source: JZ Mock A · Paper 1 · Question 17 · Publisher worked solution
knowledgePattern: Reduce a multiple-angle inequality and measure its repeated intervals

hints.title: Use one trigonometric quantity
hints.body: Treat the whole input 7x as one angle, and rewrite the double-angle cosine in terms of its sine.
hints.recap: A double-angle identity can turn a trig inequality into a quadratic inequality.
hints.pitfall: Transform the interval when renaming the angle.
hints.pause: Solve the resulting algebraic inequality within the sine range.

recall.reminder: A double-angle identity can turn a trig inequality into a quadratic inequality.

hints.title: Measure one full period
hints.body: Mark the accepted intervals during one complete sine period. Then account for all repeated periods and the input scale.
hints.recap: Total accepted length is found by adding the lengths of the allowed intervals.
hints.pitfall: An isolated equality point contributes no interval length, and the transformed variable has a different scale.
hints.pause: Calculate a full-period length and convert the total back to x.

recall.reminder: Total accepted length is found by adding the lengths of the allowed intervals.

solution:
1. Put t=7x, so 0≤t≤14π. Since cos2t=1−2sin2t, the inequality is 2sin2t+sint−1≥0.

2. Factor: (2sint−1)(sint+1)≥0. With −1≤sint≤1, this means sint≥1/2 together with the isolated values where sint=−1.

3. In each full period, the interval has length 5π/6−π/6=2π/3. The isolated points have zero length. There are seven periods in the t-interval, giving total t-length 14π/3.

4. As x=t/7, divide the length by 7: the required total is 2π/3. Answer D.
